test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 23 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If the perimeter of a circle is (88)/(7) cm, then find the perimeter (in cm) of the square the length of each of whose sides is equal to the radius of the given circle. [Use π = (22)/(7)]
solution:
**Given:**

Perimeter of the circle = 88/7 cm

π = 22/7

**Formula used:**

Perimeter (circumference) of a circle = 2πr

Perimeter of a square = 4 × side length

**Calculation:**

Given circumference: 88/7 cm

Using the formula 2πr = 88/7 

⇒2 × 22/7 × r = 88/7

⇒ r = 2 cm

The radius of the circle is 2 cm.

The side length of the square is equal to the radius of the circle, so the side length of the square = 2 cm.

Perimeter of the square = 4 × side length

⇒ Perimeter of the square = 4 × 2 cm

⇒ Perimeter of the square = 8 cm

**∴ The perimeter of the square is 8 cm**.
